vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: pixmind-image
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle provides documentation and instructions for an AI agent to interface with the Pixmind image generation API. It defines standard parameters for text-to-image and image-to-image tasks and references external helper scripts (image-generate.js and task-status.js) for execution. No malicious code, data exfiltration patterns, or prompt injection attacks were identified in the provided files (SKILL.md, _meta.json).

llm.summary: The skill claims to be a Pixmind image generator and only needs an API key, but the instructions reference an unexpected API host and non-existent helper scripts, so the package is internally inconsistent and should be verified before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description say "Pixmind" and list a single API key (PIXMIND_API_KEY) which is proportionate, but the documented endpoint (https://aihub-admin.aimix.pro/open-api/...) and example response domains (e.g., chatmix.top) do not match the claimed Pixmind branding and there is no homepage/source to confirm the provider. The listed models also include third‑party names (Imagen, Gemini) that are unlikely to be literal Pixmind models — this mismatch suggests possible mislabelling or a proxy aggregator.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is instruction-only and focuses on calling the API (OK), but it also shows usage with node scripts at {baseDir}/../../scripts/*. No code files or scripts are included in the bundle, so either the instructions assume external repository layout or would cause the agent to attempt to execute missing local scripts. The instructions otherwise do not request unrelated files or extra credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — lowest-risk delivery mechanism. Nothing will be written to disk by an installer because there is no install step.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only one environment variable (PIXMIND_API_KEY) is required, which is proportionate for an API-based image generation skill. However, because the API host is not clearly the official Pixmind domain and there is no homepage/source, handing over an API key would send it to an unverified third party unless you confirm the endpoint.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent or system-wide privileges. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (disable-model-invocation: false) which is normal and not by itself suspicious.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is internally inconsistent — it says "Pixmind" but points to an unfamiliar API host and references helper scripts that are not included. Before installing: 1) Verify the API endpoint (aihub-admin.aimix.pro) is an official Pixmind or trusted partner endpoint via vendor docs or support. 2) Do not provide a production API key until you confirm the provider; use a limited or disposable key for testing. 3) Ask the publisher for the missing scripts or prepare your own request code instead of running node {baseDir}/../../scripts/*. 4) Prefer skills with a visible homepage, source repository, or official publisher. 5) If you proceed, monitor network calls and API usage and restrict the key's permissions/quotas. If you cannot verify the endpoint or publisher, do not install or use this skill.
